blocks.text:
Lima brings together modern neighbourhoods, colonial architecture and Peruvian cooking. In Cusco, the legacy of the Inca Empire survives in the streets, temples and stonework. Machu Picchu appears amid mountains and clouds, and on Lake Titicaca life goes on aboard the floating Uros Islands. The scenery changes again after the Andes, when you travel to Puerto Maldonado and the Amazon rainforest.

The itinerary also includes Paracas, Aguas Calientes and Puerto Maldonado.

## Peru’s ancient civilisations and landscapes from the Pacific to the Amazon

This itinerary takes in several distinct sides of Peru. In Lima, the colonial centre and modern Miraflores show two sides of the capital. In the desert, you’ll see the Huacachina Oasis and fly over the Nazca Lines. Arequipa and Colca Canyon bring volcanic landscapes, hot springs and a chance to spot Andean condors.

The route then climbs to Lake Titicaca. Visit the floating Uros Islands and Taquile Island, learn about local traditions and see the high plains of the Altiplano. Follow the Sun Route to Cusco, the former capital of the Inca Empire, then continue to the Sacred Valley and Machu Picchu.

The final major leg takes you into the Peruvian Amazon. Over several days around Puerto Maldonado, you can explore the rainforest with a guide, cross suspension bridges above the forest floor, travel by canoe and boat, watch for birds and other wildlife, and learn how local communities live.
